KICKOFF — epic 6202 endowed-upset-scaup, 'Bounded disk-ceiling architecture for the Gerrit host'.

TREE (Phase 0 preflight): 6 stories, depth 2, no deeper nesting. All six carry recorded file_impact (scope=paths), so all are executable code leaves. Dependency structure is a SERIAL CHAIN, not a parallel fan-out:

    S0 7dfa livid-blondish-shearwater   Finalize the Gerrit disk-ceiling ADR        READY
     |
    S1 aa40 injurious-wellmade-moth     Isolate review-gate scratch on its own EBS  blocked by S0
     |
     +-- S2 9183 geode-joking-cockatiel   Cap Docker overlay2 + BuildKit cache      blocked by S1
     +-- S3 e956 divine-streaky-betafish  Bound journald storage                    blocked by S1
     +-- S4 2ba3 unmelted-grieving-blowfish Bound /var/tmp growth                   blocked by S1
     +-- S5 910b francium-written-squid   Bound writable container layers           blocked by S1

S2-S5 unblock TOGETHER but are NOT file-disjoint — all four touch infra/scripts/observability.sh, infra/scripts/compose-up.sh and infra/scripts/install-disk-ceilings.sh. Per the skill, parallel worktrees are only licensed for genuinely disjoint leaves, so this lands as ONE SIX-CHANGE STACK in order S0 -> S1 -> S2 -> S3 -> S4 -> S5, matching the dependency order.

LANDING METHOD (discovered, per AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md): rebar/Gerrit default. Each change pushed to refs/for/main as a stacked relation chain; every commit carries a rebar-ticket trailer plus a DCO sign-off with the commit-msg hook stamping Change-Id; two independent votes gate each change (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1); a ticket closes only after its change is Verified +1; the stack lands by submitting its top.

WORKTREE: /Users/joeoakhart/reb-6202-disk-ceiling, branch reb-6202-disk-ceiling, branched from origin/main at ebbcd7a030d6. Worktree venv confirmed first on PATH (rebar resolves to the worktree binary).

PHASE 2 IN PROGRESS: the epic claim is gated by plan-review; rebar review-plan 6202 is running. Earning the epic attestation now is deliberate — it prevents the parent-first claim cascade from hitting that same gate on the first leaf claim.

OPERATOR CONTEXT carried in: the design is firm and must not be re-litigated. Option A (per-accumulator hard caps via native GC, each capped generator carrying its OWN CloudWatch alarm) and Option C (separate EBS for review scratch) are both operator-approved. Root stays 60 GiB — headroom, not the fix. Defect 2 (alarm missing-data) stays on bug 3276 and is already landed and applied live.

comments.body:
PHASE 2 COMPLETE — epic 6202 claimed (open -> in_progress).

Plan-review needed TWO runs. The first returned INDETERMINATE with zero blocking findings and exit 2, cause `llm-degrade: NEEDS_INVESTIGATION — Unclassified failure` — LLM infrastructure, not a plan defect (prior tickets exist for the same condition on completion-verify). Retried: PASS, signed at head_sha ebbcd7a030d6029216127c83fb43c415117af366.

## Eight advisories to carry into the leaf work — four are substantive

- **G4 (real cross-ticket conflict):** S4's /var/tmp SIZE CAP conflicts with sibling 3e92 (scowlful-bovine-dragonfly), which documents `/var/tmp/rebar-evidence/<ticket>-<stamp>/` as the trap-cleaned evidence location. Capping /var/tmp without accounting for that location would either evict evidence mid-investigation or make the documented location unusable. S4 must reconcile the two — this is the kind of thing that only shows up when two tickets are read together.
- **G4 (scope overlap):** S2 and S5 share implicit state over Docker overlay2 accounting and prune behaviour. S2 caps overlay2/BuildKit; S5 bounds writable container layers — which live IN overlay2. Their caps interact and must be designed as one budget, not two independent ones.
- **G3 (coverage gap):** parent AC4 ('existing root/data disk alarms remain present; the cyclopean missing-data fix is not regressed') is NOT covered by the union of the children's ACs. No child asserts the non-regression. Needs an explicit check in whichever leaf lands last, or its own criterion.
- **T2 (the unspecified numbers):** the whole architecture rests on cap VALUES (Docker maxUsedSpace/--keep-storage, journald SystemMaxUse, /var/tmp quota, gate-scratch EBS size) and per-generator alarm thresholds that the plan does not fix. Same shape as the 9ea3 memory-limit problem: a number chosen without measurement is a guess. The measured breakdown from bug 3276 is the grounding available — root 28G of which /var/lib/docker 17G (overlay2 16G), /var/tmp 3.6G, /var/log 1.8G (journal 1.7G).
- P5 confirms independently what preflight found: S2-S5 touch the same files with no ordering edge.
- ISF: the plan does not reference this session log; cosmetic.

## Second gate memory measurement (feeds bug 9ea3 AC5)

Run 1 (degraded early): peak 752 MB / delta 501 MB / 118s. Run 2 (complete): peak 1000 MB / **delta 739 MB** / 281s. So a COMPLETE plan-review on a 6-child container ticket costs ~739 MB resident growth over ~4.7 min, and cost varies materially between runs. Recorded on 9ea3.

NEXT: claim S0 (7dfa livid-blondish-shearwater, the ADR) — the only ready leaf.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPERATOR CONSTRAINT ADDED (2026-09-03) — this changes the sizing model for S1/S2 and may expose a gap in the approved design.

Operator: '~10 plan reviews run in parallel frequently, which causes disk pressure that CANNOT be pruned until the reviews finish. That is in addition to disk pressure from code reviews and auto-deploy.'

## The code confirms the mechanism exactly

`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` documents its own design: it relies on POSIX **delete-on-last-close** plus touch-on-read mtime recency, and deliberately takes **no per-reader lease** — a PID+heartbeat lease was spiked and REJECTED as unsound (N readers per entry, PID reuse, crash-stale leases), following Gitaly/Sourcegraph/Bazel/ccache. It also skips any entry inside a short grace window.

The consequence is the operator's point, stated in the code's own terms: the janitor may UNLINK an in-flight snapshot, but under delete-on-last-close the blocks are not returned until the last reader closes. **So during peak concurrency, reclamation is structurally ineffective — the bytes are live, not garbage.**

## Why this matters for the approved design

Option A caps each accumulator via native GC at a high-water mark. **A high-water-mark GC assumes evictable data exists.** Under ~10 concurrent reviews it largely does not: the space is held by live readers and by grace-window entries. A cap set below peak concurrent hold cannot be honoured — the GC will run, find nothing evictable, and the volume fills anyway. That is the same shape as the failure this epic exists to fix: four rounds of prune-based mitigation that could not reach the bytes that mattered (~6.5 GB of orphaned overlay2 invisible to prune, per bug 3276's measurement).

So the sizing rule has to be: **cap >= peak concurrent hold**, not cap = steady-state target. And S1's dedicated gate-scratch volume must be sized for PEAK, not average.

## Two mitigating and two aggravating factors

MITIGATING: the snapshot store is CONTENT-ADDRESSED, so N concurrent reviews against the same base share one snapshot rather than holding N copies. And snapshots stream to disk with a 512 MiB cap per `workflow/snapshot.py`.
AGGRAVATING: the review-bot CLONE is per-review and not shared — `voter.py:381` opens `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='reviewbot-')` per review, so clones scale linearly with concurrency. And the operator notes code reviews and auto-deploy add pressure on the same volume concurrently.

## The design gap this exposes — needs an operator decision

The approved design (Option A caps + Option C separate volume) contains **no admission control**. If peak concurrent demand exceeds the provisioned volume, no cap value can help — the choices are a volume sized for peak, or a limit on how many reviews may hold scratch at once. Sizing for peak alone is unbounded in principle: the ceiling becomes 'however many reviews someone launches'.

Recorded as an open question rather than decided, since the design is operator-approved and this is a genuine addition to it, not a re-litigation.

## Also settles the bug 9ea3 OOM arithmetic

A COMPLETE plan-review measured today at ~739 MB resident delta. Ten in parallel is ~7.4 GB on an 8 GiB box already carrying gerrit 0.88 GB + mcp 1.08 GB + review-bot 0.17 GB + opcert 0.04 GB. That is a definitive OOM explanation and closes the gap I flagged earlier, where a single ~500 MB gate against ~2.3 GiB headroom did not account for the kill.

═══ HANDOFF FOR CONTEXT COMPACTION (2026-09-03) — read this first ═══

## ROLE
Debug orchestrator: owns all UNPARENTED bugs, plus epic 6202 as of this session. Drives work via subagents; does not implement directly. Parallel sessions own three other epics.

## CLOSED THIS SESSION (4 orphan bugs, 12 changes merged)
- **febd** curbable-regardable-lemming — uv required-version ==0.12.7 vs floating uv:latest broke EVERY container build; the box could not deploy at all. Closed class=regression, caused_by 56b7. Changes 2558 (fix + guard), 2584 (alarm description cap).
- **3a02** lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird — MCP models under-declared 41 schema properties; baseline drained. Change 2556.
- **4f59** infertile-mindful-rodent — argparse colorization on py3.14. Change 2568. Scope was far larger than filed: 25 failures across 9 modules, TWO of them product regressions (stale generated help artifacts; usage wrapping on ANSI-inflated length).
- **f0d1** neutral-skyblue-hog — select_from_corpus eager per-ticket compile. Change 2590. ~110x: 74.2s vs ~2h15m.

## LIVE IN PRODUCTION (applied, verified)
- 12 rebar/host alarms flipped to treat_missing_data=breaching with anti-flap windows (bff5, change 2551).
-  on mcp_healthy — the MCP outage was invisible for 12h; it is not now (9ea3, changes 2565+2584).
-  on data_disk_debris_bytes, 1 GiB threshold, reading 0 (3276 AC5, change 2586).
- Memory instrumentation: mem_available_percent / mem_used_percent / mem_probe_ok / container_memory_rss_bytes (4 stable service dims) / container_stats_ok, plus the GATE_PEAK_RSS marker (9ea3, change 2589).

## OPEN BUGS — state and what each needs
- **3276** cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin — 5 of 6 ACs met. AC1 ticked via operator-accepted REPLAY (induced publish-stop rejected as 12-alarm noise). Only **AC4 (bounded ceiling) remains, owned by epic 6202**. Closes when the epic delivers, or on an operator decision to attribute AC4 to the epic.
- **bff5** herbal-garish-monkey — AC2 REWRITTEN and MET by replay (operator principle: an AC that depends on time passing is defective). 24h replay: 27 missing periods absorbed, ZERO missing-data transitions; 3 alarms transitioned, all TRUE POSITIVES. Remaining: AC3 induced fetch-failure on mirror_out_of_sync, AC6 enumeration.
- **9ea3** witted-invisible-roan — AC1/AC2/AC3 met, AC4 landed. **OOM arithmetic now SETTLED**: operator states ~10 plan reviews run in parallel; 10 x ~739 MB + 2.17 GB steady state = ~9.6 GB on an 8 GiB host. AC5 needs a box-side gate measurement (today's numbers are from a LOCAL CLI run).

## EPIC 6202 — claimed, in progress
Title: 'Bounded disk-ceiling architecture for the Gerrit host'. Claimed (attestation PASS at ebbcd7a030d6, needed a retry after an llm-degrade INDETERMINATE).

**Tree is a SERIAL CHAIN, 7 stories.** S2-S5 are NOT file-disjoint (all touch observability.sh, compose-up.sh, install-disk-ceilings.sh), so this lands as ONE STACK, not parallel worktrees:

    S0 7dfa livid-blondish-shearwater      ADR 0110                         READY, review-plan running
     +- S6 09da grusome-ecumenical-polarbear  fast-fail gate admission      NEW this session
     |    +- S2 9183 geode-joking-cockatiel    Docker overlay2 + BuildKit cap
     |    +- S3 e956 divine-streaky-betafish   journald SystemMaxUse
     |    +- S4 2ba3 unmelted-grieving-blowfish /var/tmp
     |    +- S5 910b francium-written-squid    writable container layers
     +- S1 aa40 injurious-wellmade-moth      dedicated gate-scratch EBS

**S6 is new and load-bearing.** Operator input: ~10 parallel reviews. janitor.py relies on POSIX delete-on-last-close and takes NO reader lease (a PID+heartbeat lease was spiked and REJECTED as unsound). So it can unlink an in-flight snapshot but the blocks do not return until the last reader closes — under peak concurrency the held bytes are LIVE, not garbage, and a high-water-mark GC has nothing to evict. **A cap below peak concurrent hold cannot be honoured**, which is why S6 gates S2-S5. Design: configurable limit shared by plan-review AND completion-verifier (both snapshot the repo at a ref); at capacity FAST-FAIL with a congestion message, never queue — a queued gate still holds its thread and ~739 MB.

**Operator decisions carried:** Option A + C approved, do not re-litigate. Every capped generator gets its own alarm. Root stays 60 GiB (headroom, not the fix). Cap values = measured defaults, settable by config.

**Gate advisories still to honour:** epic AC4 (3276 non-regression) is covered by NO child; S2/S5 overlap (writable layers live in overlay2 — one budget, not two); S4 conflicts with 3e92's /var/tmp/rebar-evidence location.

## IN FLIGHT — 3 subagents, none pushed
1. **reb-split-sizing** (change 2593, Verified -1): fixing a REAL breakage — test_review_discovery_architecture._PROJECTION_BUILDERS hardcodes sizing.py and asserts it constructs DiscoveryStagePlan; the split moved that to checkpoints.py.
2. **reb-split-composer** (change 2594, Verified -1): classifying an e2e worker crash (test_editor_e2e gw0 crashed). Evidence it is NOT the split: passes on clean main locally, and the identical crash hit 2593, an independent change. Must be classified, not rechecked — project policy forbids retry-as-fix.
3. **reb-6202-disk-ceiling**: drafting ADR 0110 (S0). Not committed; awaiting S0's claim.

**Change 2596** (acli.py split, 800->567) was CI-running at handoff — check it.

## MODULE SPLITS — all three at-cap modules done
2593 sizing 800->547 (+budget 168, +checkpoints 144); 2594 composer 800->508 (composer_edit 188->490); 2596 acli 800->567 (acli_rest 340->585). **No src/rebar file is at the 800 cap now.** Nine remain at 794-799 — next batch if wanted.

## CARRY-OVERS not acted on
minio:latest in docker-compose.langfuse.yml; bridge suggest-mapping's parser built outside the RebarArgumentParser family (_cli/__init__.py:147); autodeploy.sh is 1313 lines and UNGATED (module-size gate is src/rebar Python only) — two defects found in it this session.

## RECURRING HAZARDS (cost time this session)
- **/tmp is shared across parallel agents** — one clobbered another's backup mid-proof. Use the worktree or CLAUDE_JOB_DIR.
- **Test harness guards fail if repo HEAD moves mid-sweep** — do not commit during a full suite run.
- **'Missing tree' push rejection = STALE BASE, not corruption.** Rebase onto the current gerrit tip; recurred twice.
- **git commit --amend --no-edit produces NO_CODE_CHANGE** and Gerrit COPIES a -1 forward instead of re-reviewing. Use  (CONTRIBUTING §2) to re-trigger, not a manufactured edit.
- **make amend-msg amends the MESSAGE ONLY** — verify with git show --stat that code edits are in the commit.
- **origin (GitHub) lags gerrit** — fetch from gerrit after a submit or you get a stale tree.

CORRECTION to the handoff entry above — three names were lost to shell backtick substitution when it was written. Restoring them verbatim:

1. The MCP serving-path alarm applied to production is named:
       rebar-mcp-serving-path-down
   metric mcp_healthy, Statistic Minimum, threshold 1.0 LessThanThreshold, period 300, EP 3, DTA 2, treat_missing_data breaching. State OK. Healthy is defined as HTTP 401 exactly (auth challenge) — a 200 means the auth middleware is not running and is itself worth paging for.

2. The /var/gerrit debris alarm applied to production is named:
       rebar-gerrit-data-disk-debris
   metric data_disk_debris_bytes, dimensions InstanceId + mount=/var/gerrit, threshold 1073741824 (1 GiB), EP 3, DTA 2, treat_missing_data breaching. State OK, publishing 0.0 every 5 minutes.

3. The documented way to re-trigger a Gerrit LLM review WITHOUT pushing a new patch set is to comment:
       rerun-llm-review
   on the change (CONTRIBUTING.md section 2). This matters because `git commit --amend --no-edit` produces a NO_CODE_CHANGE patch set whose copy condition CARRIES A -1 FORWARD rather than re-reviewing. Earlier in this session I worked around that by manufacturing a real content edit; that was unnecessary and is the wrong habit.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
S0 ADR DRAFTED (uncommitted) — docs/adr/0111-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture.md, 257 lines, plus .numbers/0111 and a one-line README index entry. All gates green: check_docs_index rc=0, check_adr_numbers rc=0, gen_adr_index --check rc=0, make lint rc=0, 27 tests passed.

## FOUR corrections to what I briefed — record these, two matter beyond this story

1. **ADR 0110 was already taken.** docs/adr/0110-change-shape-advisory-not-blocking.md landed on origin/main in commit 8f19115cf2fb (2026-09-01), AFTER the epic was planned. The story's plan asserted "highest current number is 0109" and the plan-review gate BLOCKED on exactly that. Corrected to 0111 everywhere. Reusable lesson: a plan that pins an ADR number at authoring time goes stale silently, because other work allocates numbers meanwhile. The gate caught it only because it RE-DERIVED the fact instead of trusting the plan's assertion.

2. **The slug had to change too, for a non-obvious reason.** gen_adr_index.py buckets ADRs by FIRST-MATCHING KEYWORD in slug order, and "gerrit" is claimed by the earlier "Git / Gerrit workflow" group — so 0110-gerrit-disk-ceiling-... would have filed an INFRA adr under Gerrit workflow. Renamed to 0111-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture ("on-box" is an Infra & deploy keyword, alongside 0079/0104/0105). Verified it renders under Infra & deploy.

3. **I OVERSTATED the no-upsize constraint, repeatedly, including to the operator.** I had been saying "ADR 0079 and 0104 explicitly decided against upsizing to t4g.xlarge" as though it were a standing prohibition on instance type. It is narrower than that: both ADRs say the SAME sentence, that overlap is capped one-in/one-out "guarded by a memory-pressure alarm, so the transient 2x rebar-mcp never forces the t4g.large up to t4g.xlarge". That is MEMORY-scoped and specific to MCP DEPLOY OVERLAP. Neither ADR says anything about root volume size, and neither is a general bar on resizing the host. The ADR therefore declines the resize ON ITS OWN MERITS (an unbounded generator fills any volume) and records the t4g.large constraint separately WITH its exact scope. My stronger framing should not be repeated.

4. src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py (not src/rebar/reviewbot/); line 381 confirmed.

## TWO findings that strengthen the design and change S6's shape

- **A fast-fail admission seam ALREADY EXISTS.** src/rebar/review_bot/low_disk.py plus janitor.py's ensure_min_free_space / SnapshotLowDiskError / DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_GIB already REFUSE before cloning, on a free-space floor. So S6 should extend that seam with a second term (a concurrency counter) rather than introducing a parallel admission mechanism. This materially simplifies S6 and avoids a new mechanism the ratchet would count.
- **REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR already parameterises the snapshot store's base dir**, so Option C (dedicated gate-scratch volume) is largely CONFIG, not code.
- Also: the per-generator-alarm constraint is an argument from repo history, not preference — rebar-root-disk-pressure already existed at 85% with treat_missing_data=breaching (bug ac14, after incident 2731) and did NOT prevent 3276, because it can only say "root disk high" and never names the saturated generator.

## ADR decision summary (7 decisions)

(1) per-accumulator hard caps at each consumer's native GC; (2) every capped generator carries its own alarm, demoting root-disk-pressure to backstop; (3) gate scratch on a dedicated EBS volume; (4) root stays 60 GiB as headroom not fix; (5) bounded concurrency with FAST-FAIL admission — one shared counter for plan-review and completion-verifier, refusal not queueing, and on the review-bot path it follows ADR 0069's retryable-deferral shape and MAY NEVER BECOME AN LLM-Review -1; (6) caps are measured defaults settable via [snapshot]/REBAR_GATE_* and terraform vars, never constants; (7) host sizing not reopened.

Load-bearing argument, built as a symmetry: prune could not reach 6.5 GB of orphaned overlay2 (~1.06 GB ceiling vs a 29 GB problem), and a watermark GC cannot reach bytes held open by live readers. Both reclaimers pointed at structurally unreachable bytes. Bounded concurrency is therefore a PRECONDITION for the caps, not an addition to them.

## Consequence noted for later: the root_disk_pressure alarm DESCRIPTION still says "The box's 30G ROOT disk" while var.root_volume_size_gb is 60. Cosmetic but misleading during an incident.

NEXT ACTION: re-run review-plan on S0 now the 0110->0111 correction has landed in the ticket, then claim S0 and commit the drafted ADR.
